title: Record Water on the Manning
location: Taree–Wingham, Manning River, New South Wales, Australia
headline: Follow Taree–Wingham, Manning River, New South Wales, Australia across 4 real radar observations
introduction: From 20–25 May 2025 a slow-moving trough produced a documented 1-in-500-year flood on the NSW Mid North Coast. The Manning River at Taree peaked near 6.4 m on 21 May, above the 1929 record, with major flooding at Wingham and widespread rescues. These four Sentinel-1 radar visits follow a focused Manning corridor around Taree and Wingham from before the crest through late June.
conclusion: The 21 May acquisition falls on the documented crest day at Taree; it is still a radar brightness map, not a measured water depth or validated inundation polygon. Later frames show follow-up landscape response and must not be read as a full recovery certificate. Standing water, wet soil, crops and viewing geometry all affect brightness. No flood-area accuracy or damage estimate is claimed.

properties.name: Taree–Wingham, Manning River, New South Wales, Australia
properties.scope: Focused river corridor, not the entire disaster

method: Sentinel-1 RTC, consistent polarization and orbit per story. Source calibrated power converted using 10*log10 where necessary; existing dB sources are not converted again. Bilinear alignment to the first grid, invalid/nonpositive power masked, fixed viridis −30 to +5 dB display. Statistics are radar response, not classified flood area.
eventEvidence: Documented by NSW SES, ABC News and the 2025 NSW floods summary; radar observations are not a validated flood classification.
